purpose: Section 4: a stable, pre-compilation, sibling-safe claim identity - never sectionRef alone.

primaryIdentitySource.derivation: Content-derived from (documentId + anchor span + detection signature) - already proven, already shipped, already used at Phase 3E scale across FWRG/LSB/CONMED.
primaryIdentitySource.whyThisDistinguishesSiblings: Anchor span (structuralNodeId + charStart/charEnd) is occurrence-safe per Phase 3F.1.2's structural-identity work - two sibling sub-provisions under the same base section have distinct anchors and therefore distinct semanticUnitIds, even when they'd share an identical human-readable sectionRef prefix.
primaryIdentitySource.namespacePrefix: su: (see identity.ts's claimKeyFromSemanticUnit) - prevents a coincidental string collision between this scheme and the fallback scheme below from silently merging two unrelated claims.

fallbackIdentitySource.source: The compiler's own candidateRef convention (SemanticCompilerInput.candidateRef's own documented rule): a Phase 2B DiscoveredCandidate.discoveryId where one exists, else the normalized source section ref.
fallbackIdentitySource.whenUsed: Only when no semantic-coverage unit has been built yet for this claim (e.g. a hypothetical future emission point wired directly at the compiler/verifier stage rather than the coverage auditor - not used by this phase's own single wired emission point, which always has a MaterialSemanticUnit available, but reserved for forward compatibility).
fallbackIdentitySource.residualRiskDisclosed: candidateRef's OWN fallback (when no discoveryId exists) can in principle still collide across two sibling sub-provisions discovery never separately distinguished - the exact same class of risk Workstream A's evaluator fix addressed for the frozen matcher in Phase 3F.1.5.3. This module does not attempt to re-solve that risk (Section 20 forbids casually reopening the frozen evaluator matcher, and the fallback path is unused by this phase's actual wiring anyway). Per Section 31, a claim identified only through this degraded fallback path, with no discoveryId, is closer to the 'undiscovered claim' case this architecture explicitly does not claim to solve.

designAlternativesConsidered.alternative: Invent a brand-new claim-identity scheme from scratch for this phase.
designAlternativesConsidered.rejected: Directly contradicts Section 4's own instruction and the established discipline throughout this codebase's history (Phase 3F.1.2's ARCH-PROP work exists specifically because inventing parallel identity schemes has caused real defects before).
Section 4 explicitly forbids this - does not distinguish sibling/sub-provisions under the same base section.

designAlternativesConsidered.alternative: Use a fresh random id per detection.
designAlternativesConsidered.rejected: Breaks Section 11's dedup requirement entirely - every detection would look like a new claim.
